full_judgment: 2. The relevant facts, for disposal of this petition, in short, are that the plaintiff-respondents instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession alleging, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Baidyaram Sarker and Raj Mohan Sarker in equal share. Raj Mohan died leaving behind one son Raj Kanta and daughter Joshoda and wife Furkuni. Baidyaram Sarker died leaving behind brother's son Raj Kanta. Thereby Raj Kanta acquired title in 16 annas share of the suit property and, thereafter, he died leaving his mother Furkuni, wife Konok. Prova and sister's sons Subal Chandra Sarker and Khagendra Nath Sarker. After the death of Raj Kanta his wife konok Prova embraced Islam and had married with a Muslim and thereby lost her right of inheritance in the property left by Raj Kanta. Kanak Prova sold 'Ka' scheduled property to Subarna Lata Das and Sandhya Rani by a deed dated 11.10.1946. They again got a sale deed executed by Furkani on 14.12.1946. Those deeds were void because Furkani had no legal necessity. Sandhya Rani and others settled some portion of the land to defendants. Furkuni died on 18.03.1973. The plaintiffs are the evisioners and they have inherited the entire property left by Rajkanta. Subornalata and Sandhya Rani did not acquire any interest in the suit land. The plaintiffs demanded possession of the suit land in 1386 B.S. but they did not pay any heed. Hence was the suit.
